import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 730

*References:*
  - [erdosproblems.com/730](https://www.erdosproblems.com/730)
  - [A129515](https://oeis.org/A129515)
-/
namespace Erdos730

abbrev S :=
  {(n, m) : ℕ × ℕ | n < m ∧ n.centralBinom.primeFactors = m.centralBinom.primeFactors}


/--
Are there infinitely many pairs of integers $n < m$ such that $\binom{2n}{n}$
and $\binom{2m}{m}$ have the same set of prime divisors?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_730 : answer(sorry) ↔ S.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
For example, $(87,88)$ and $(607,608)$ are such pairs.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_730.variants.explicit_pairs :
    {(87, 88), (607, 608)} ⊆ S := by
  rintro _ (rfl | rfl) <;> exact ⟨by decide, by native_decide⟩

/--
There are examples where $(n, m) ∈ S$ with $m ≠ n + 1$.

(Found by AlphaProof, although it was implicit already in [A129515])
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_730.variants.delta_ne_one : ∃ (n m : ℕ), (n, m) ∈ S ∧ m ≠ n + 1 := by
  dsimp [S]
  use 10003
  use 10005
  norm_num [Finset.ext_iff, Nat.choose_eq_zero_iff, Nat.centralBinom]
  simp_rw [Nat.choose_eq_descFactorial_div_factorial]
  intro p hp
  constructor
  all_goals exact fun h' => or_self_iff.1 (hp.dvd_mul.1 (
    h'.trans (by refine' of_decide_eq_true (by constructor : _ = ↑_))))


end Erdos730

status_issues.source_status: Solved affirmatively. The Erdős Problems page credits GPT Pro, prompted by Price. Its linked manuscript, dated June 24, 2026, proves infinitely many consecutive pairs, a stronger result than the stated problem.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/730 now displays SOLVED and says, 'This was solved by GPT Pro (prompted by Price)'. The linked manuscript https://www.overleaf.com/read/gpttrsmhbhbk#a7cfdf, Theorem 1.1, concludes: 'there are infinitely many consecutive pairs of central binomial coefficients having the same set of prime divisors.' The community database also lists problem 730 as solved.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to research solved, replace answer(sorry) with answer(True), and cite the linked solution. The predicate S.Infinite needs no change.

reformulations.difference: The definition uses natural-number indices without an explicit positivity hypothesis and expresses equality of prime-divisor sets as equality of Nat.primeFactors finsets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every central binomial coefficient is nonzero, so membership in its primeFactors finset is exactly primeness together with divisibility. Moreover, centralBinom 0 = 1 has no prime factors, whereas centralBinom m is even for every m > 0. Thus no pair (0,m) belongs to S, and m = 0 is already excluded by n < m. Consequently S is exactly the set of positive n < m for which every prime divides one central binomial coefficient iff it divides the other. The set equality and the resulting equivalence of infinitude statements were proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

review.notes: Checked S and all three theorems. Lean computations confirmed (87,88) and (607,608), and enumeration below 100 returned only (87,88). Independent computations using factorial prime valuations confirmed the nonconsecutive witness (10003,10005), as well as both consecutive pairs in the triple 10003,10004,10005. Both existing variant proofs have no sorryAx dependency. Scratch checks compiled without errors; the reviewed problem file was not modified.
